edges.mechanism: Resveratrol 1 g/d for 4 weeks inhibited CYP3A4 (buspirone probe) in healthy volunteers; intestinal CYP inhibition may reduce first-pass metabolism and raise exposure to co-administered substrates.
edges.evidence: Human phenotyping study (n=42) plus review; interaction magnitude at <=500 mg/d unknown

edges.mechanism: Sirolimus is a CYP3A4 substrate; resveratrol 1 g/d inhibits CYP3A4 and may raise sirolimus exposure. No direct study.
edges.evidence: Inferred from human CYP phenotyping study and review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: CYP2C9 activity (losartan probe) inhibited at 1 g/d; may raise exposure to CYP2C9 substrates such as S-warfarin.
edges.evidence: Human phenotyping study; no clinical interaction outcome study

edges.mechanism: CYP2D6 activity (dextromethorphan probe) inhibited at 1 g/d.
edges.evidence: Human phenotyping study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: CYP1A2 activity (caffeine probe) induced at 1 g/d; exposure to CYP1A2 substrates may fall.
edges.evidence: Human phenotyping study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Resveratrol 1 g/d induced CYP1A2, measured by caffeine metabolism; faster caffeine clearance possible.
edges.evidence: Human phenotyping study using caffeine as probe

edges.mechanism: CYP2C9 inhibition (warfarin pathway) plus in vitro/ex vivo antiplatelet activity (reduced TXA2, thrombus formation, collagen/epinephrine aggregation) could increase bleeding tendency.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic/ex vivo plus human CYP data; no clinical bleeding reports identified

edges.mechanism: Resveratrol inhibits COX-1-dependent and collagen/epinephrine-induced platelet aggregation; additive antiplatelet effect possible.
edges.evidence: In vitro and ex vivo platelet studies; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Additive platelet inhibition: resveratrol inhibited aggregation of platelets from aspirin-resistant patients, and a resveratrol-containing polyphenol mixture potentiated sub-inhibitory aspirin at COX-1.
edges.evidence: Ex vivo/in vitro and mouse data; no clinical bleeding data

edges.mechanism: Both resveratrol and quercetin inhibit arachidonic-acid-induced platelet aggregation via COX-1; additive antiplatelet effect plausible.
edges.evidence: In vitro functional and modelling study

edges.mechanism: Phase 2 trial of micronized resveratrol (SRT501, 5 g/d) alone or with bortezomib in relapsed/refractory myeloma was terminated after unexpected cast nephropathy/renal failure; etiology ambiguous (nausea/vomiting-related dehydration proposed).
edges.evidence: Terminated phase 2 trial (n=24) as reported by review and registry

edges.mechanism: High-dose SRT501 associated with renal failure in myeloma patients, who already have high baseline renal risk; high-dose renal toxicity also seen in rats.
edges.evidence: Terminated phase 2 trial; rat toxicology (nephropathy at 3000 mg/kg/d)

edges.mechanism: Gram-level doses linked to renal failure in myeloma and nephropathy in rats; in general populations a 31-RCT MA showed no harm (BUN slightly lower).
edges.evidence: Mixed: trial termination and animal data vs reassuring MA; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Resveratrol binds estrogen receptor and acts as an agonist/superagonist, stimulating ER+ breast cancer cell proliferation in vitro.
edges.evidence: In vitro only; relevance at achievable plasma levels unproven

edges.mechanism: Additive glucose-lowering via AMPK/SIRT1-related pathways; the combination lowered fasting glucose more than resveratrol alone in a PCOS RCT with no unexpected toxicity.
edges.evidence: One 6-month RCT (n=63) and preclinical SR; resveratrol glycemic effect itself small and inconsistent

edges.mechanism: Modest reductions in glucose/HbA1c/insulin in diabetic participants could add to antidiabetic drugs.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs; low certainty and inconsistent

edges.mechanism: Proposed complementary SIRT1 support: NAD+ precursors supply SIRT1 substrate while resveratrol is proposed as an allosteric activator. Human SIRT1 not measurably changed by resveratrol.
edges.evidence: Narrative review rationale only; no human combination trial; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: NR plus resveratrol outperformed either alone in diabetic rat wound healing; complementary NAD+/SIRT1 rationale.
edges.evidence: Rat study and narrative review; no human data

edges.mechanism: 250 mg/d blunted training gains in VO2max, BP and lipids and blunted reductions in muscle oxidative stress/TNF-alpha in aged men; another RCT with 500 mg/d found enhanced muscle adaptations.
edges.evidence: Small RCTs with conflicting results; low certainty

edges.mechanism: ALT/AST rose with resveratrol in an NAFLD RCT and ALT increased in an MA; no consistent benefit on liver parameters.
edges.evidence: RCT and MA of 7 RCTs; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Physiological (not analytical) elevation of aminotransferases reported in NAFLD trials.
edges.evidence: RCT and MA
